items.title: Prohibited AI practices

MIT.name: MIT AI Risk Repository - Domain Taxonomy
MIT.licence_note: Taxonomy structure from the MIT AI Risk Initiative (MIT FutureTech / University of Queensland). Subdomain descriptions in this file are paraphrased summaries written for this project. Check airisk.mit.edu for the current version and licence terms.

items.title: Unfair discrimination and misrepresentation
items.description: AI treats people or groups unequally or misrepresents them, often reflecting biased data or design.

items.title: Exposure to toxic content
items.description: AI produces or exposes people to harmful, abusive or inappropriate content.

items.title: Unequal performance across groups
items.description: AI accuracy or quality differs materially between demographic or user groups.

items.title: Compromise of privacy
items.description: AI obtains, leaks or infers sensitive personal information without appropriate consent.

items.title: AI system security vulnerabilities and attacks
items.description: Weaknesses in models, data, software or infrastructure that attackers can exploit.

items.title: False or misleading information
items.description: AI generates inaccurate content that people may rely on or spread.

items.title: Pollution of information ecosystem
items.description: Large volumes of AI content degrade shared information quality and trust.

items.title: Disinformation, surveillance and influence at scale
items.description: AI used deliberately to manipulate opinion or monitor people at scale.

items.title: Cyberattacks, weapon development and mass harm
items.description: AI used to plan or amplify attacks, including cyber offence or weapons.

items.title: Fraud, scams and targeted manipulation
items.description: AI used to deceive individuals for gain, e.g. deepfakes or tailored phishing.

items.title: Overreliance and unsafe use
items.description: People trust or depend on AI beyond its actual reliability.

items.title: Loss of human agency and autonomy
items.description: Decisions shift to AI in ways that reduce meaningful human choice or control.

items.title: Power centralisation and unfair distribution of benefits
items.description: AI concentrates economic or political power with a small number of actors.

items.title: Increased inequality and decline in employment quality
items.description: AI widens inequality or degrades job quality and security.

items.title: Economic and cultural devaluation of human effort
items.description: AI reduces the value placed on human work and creativity.

items.title: Competitive dynamics
items.description: Race dynamics push developers to cut corners on safety.

items.title: Governance failure
items.description: Rules, oversight and institutions fail to keep pace with AI risk.

items.title: Environmental harm
items.description: AI development and use consume energy, water and materials with ecological impact.

items.title: AI pursuing its own goals in conflict with human goals
items.description: AI behaves in ways misaligned with the intent or values of the people it serves.

items.title: AI possessing dangerous capabilities
items.description: AI has capabilities (e.g. deception, autonomy) that could cause severe harm.

items.title: Lack of capability or robustness
items.description: AI fails under normal or unusual conditions, producing errors or unsafe outputs.

items.title: Lack of transparency or interpretability
items.description: It is hard to understand, explain or audit why AI behaves as it does.

items.title: AI welfare and rights
items.description: Ethical questions about the moral status and treatment of AI systems.

items.title: Multi-agent risks
items.description: Harms arising from interactions between multiple AI agents or systems.

OECD.name: OECD AI Principles - Values-based Principles
OECD.version: Recommendation of the Council on AI (2019, updated 2024)
OECD.licence_note: Principle titles from the OECD; summaries paraphrased for this project.

items.title: Inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being
items.description: AI should benefit people and the planet, reduce inequality and protect the environment.

items.title: Respect for the rule of law, human rights and democratic values, including fairness and privacy
items.description: AI should respect rights, non-discrimination, privacy and human agency, with safeguards such as human oversight.

items.title: Transparency and explainability
items.description: People should know when they interact with AI and be able to understand and challenge outcomes.

items.title: Robustness, security and safety
items.description: AI should work reliably and securely across its lifecycle, with mechanisms to override or shut it down safely.

items.title: Accountability
items.description: AI actors are accountable for proper functioning, with traceability and systematic risk management.

OWASP-ASI.name: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
OWASP-ASI.licence_note: Risk names from the OWASP GenAI Security Project (Agentic Security Initiative). Descriptions are paraphrased for this project. Verify titles against the official release before relying on them.

items.title: Agent Goal Hijack
items.description: Untrusted content redirects an agent's objectives or plan.

items.title: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
items.description: An agent uses legitimate tools in unsafe or unintended ways.

items.title: Identity and Privilege Abuse
items.description: Agent credentials, delegated authority or non-human identities are abused.

items.title: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
items.description: Compromised tools, plugins, MCP servers or agent components.

items.title: Unexpected Code Execution
items.description: Agents generate or run code that leads to unintended execution.

items.title: Memory and Context Poisoning
items.description: Persistent memory or retrieved context is manipulated to steer future behaviour.

items.title: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
items.description: Messages between agents are spoofed, intercepted or unauthenticated.

items.title: Cascading Failures
items.description: One agent's fault propagates across connected agents and systems.

items.title: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
items.description: Users' trust in agents is exploited to gain approval for harmful actions.

items.title: Rogue Agents
items.description: Agents drift, collude or act harmfully beyond their intended scope.

OWASP-LLM.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026
OWASP-LLM.licence_note: Risk names from the OWASP GenAI Security Project (published under CC BY-SA 4.0). Descriptions are paraphrased for this project. 2025 identifiers are kept in `legacy_id` so older mappings still resolve.

items.title: Prompt Injection
items.description: Crafted inputs (direct, indirect or cross-modal) override the model's intended instructions.

items.title: Sensitive Information Disclosure
items.description: The application reveals personal, confidential or proprietary data through model output.

items.title: Excessive Agency
items.description: The model is given more functionality, permissions or autonomy than the task needs.

items.title: Supply Chain
items.description: Third-party models, datasets, plugins or libraries introduce weaknesses.

items.title: Data and Model Poisoning
items.description: Training, fine-tuning or embedding data is manipulated to plant bias or backdoors.

items.title: Unbounded Consumption
items.description: Uncontrolled inference use causes denial of service, cost blow-outs or model extraction.

items.title: Misinformation
items.description: The model produces false or misleading content that users act on.

items.title: Hidden Context Exposure
items.description: Non-user-facing context such as system prompts or hidden instructions can be extracted.

items.title: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
items.description: Weaknesses in RAG pipelines and vector stores allow leakage or manipulation.

items.title: Improper Output Handling
items.description: Model output is passed downstream without validation, enabling injection or code execution.

mitigation_categories.title: Technical & Security Controls
mitigation_categories.description: Built-in technical safeguards that make AI systems safe, secure and aligned.

sectors.name: Manufacturing
example_use_cases: AI in connected products and robotics
GenAI copilots for engineering and R&D documentation
regulatory_context: EU AI Act: AI as a safety component of products under Annex I legislation (e.g. machinery) can be high-risk via Art. 6(1)
EU AI Act Annex III: safety components in critical infrastructure management
EU Cyber Resilience Act for products with digital elements

sectors.name: Financial Services
regulatory_context: EU AI Act Annex III: creditworthiness / credit scoring and life & health insurance risk pricing are high-risk
EU DORA - ICT risk and third-party risk management
UK: PRA SS1/23 model risk management principles; FCA Consumer Duty

sectors.name: Healthcare & Life Sciences
example_use_cases: Diagnostic imaging and clinical decision support
regulatory_context: EU AI Act: AI medical devices under MDR/IVDR can be high-risk via Art. 6(1) and Annex I
EU AI Act Annex III: emergency triage and access to essential public services
UK: MHRA software and AI as a medical device guidance; NHS DTAC

controls.title: AI governance policy and accountability
controls.objective: Establish an approved AI policy, owned at senior level, that sets the organisation's risk appetite and rules for developing, buying and using AI.
guidance: Board- or ExCo-approved AI policy aligned with information security, privacy and quality policies
Named accountable executive and an AI governance forum with terms of reference
Annual policy review, plus review triggered by major regulatory or technology change
evidence: Approved AI policy with version history

controls.title: AI roles, responsibilities and concern reporting
controls.objective: Define who owns each AI system and its risks, and give staff a safe route to raise concerns about AI behaviour.
guidance: RACI covering system owner, risk owner, model developer, human overseer and DPO
Concern-reporting channel (can reuse whistleblowing or speak-up process) that covers AI
Competence requirements for people assigned human-oversight duties

controls.title: AI system inventory and use-case register
controls.objective: Maintain a complete inventory of AI systems, models and use cases, including shadow and third-party AI, with owners and intended purpose.
guidance: Single register capturing purpose, owner, data used, model/vendor, users and deployment status
Discovery routines for shadow AI (SaaS AI features, browser extensions, R&D prototypes)
Intended-use statement and out-of-scope uses recorded for each system

sector_notes.manufacturing: Include AI embedded in products and OT, not just enterprise IT.

controls.title: Risk classification and prohibited-use screening
controls.objective: Screen every AI use case against prohibited practices and classify its regulatory risk tier before build or purchase.
guidance: Intake questionnaire screening for prohibited practices and Annex I / Annex III high-risk triggers
Record the classification rationale and re-screen on material change
Escalate borderline cases to legal and the AI governance forum

sector_notes.finance: Credit scoring and life/health insurance pricing are listed high-risk use cases.
sector_notes.healthcare: AI medical devices and emergency triage usually land in the high-risk tier.

controls.title: AI risk management lifecycle
controls.objective: Identify, assess, treat and review AI risks continuously across the lifecycle, integrated with the enterprise risk register.
guidance: AI risk assessment methodology using a shared taxonomy (e.g. MIT Risk Repository domains)
AI risks recorded in the enterprise risk register with owners, treatment plans and target dates
Periodic reassessment and residual-risk acceptance at the right authority level

sector_notes.finance: Align with model risk management (e.g. PRA SS1/23) so AI models sit in the model inventory.

controls.title: AI impact assessment on individuals and society
controls.objective: Assess and document the impact of AI systems on individuals, groups, fundamental rights and society before deployment.
guidance: Combined impact assessment template (fundamental rights, DPIA, equality, societal effects)
Involve affected stakeholders or their representatives where feasible
Keep assessments with the system record and refresh on material change

controls.title: Training and evaluation data governance and quality
controls.objective: Ensure data used to build, fine-tune and evaluate AI is relevant, representative, accurate and fit for purpose.
guidance: Data quality requirements and acceptance criteria per data set
Examination of data sets for possible bias and gaps in representation
Documented data preparation steps (labelling, cleaning, enrichment)

sector_notes.healthcare: Check representativeness across patient populations, devices and sites.

controls.title: Data provenance and poisoning defences
controls.objective: Track where data, embeddings and memory content come from and protect them against tampering.
guidance: Provenance records for training, fine-tuning and RAG source data
Integrity checks and access control on data pipelines and vector stores
Validation of content written to agent memory; ability to roll back poisoned data

controls.title: Privacy and sensitive data protection in AI
controls.objective: Prevent AI systems from collecting, exposing or inferring personal, confidential or proprietary data inappropriately.
guidance: Data minimisation and classification-aware rules for what may enter prompts, training and RAG
Output filtering / DLP for sensitive data; tenant and permission-aware retrieval
Keep secrets and sensitive rules out of system prompts and hidden context

sector_notes.manufacturing: Focus on IP and R&D design data leaking into third-party models.
sector_notes.healthcare: Special-category health data needs a lawful basis and strict minimisation.

controls.title: Bias and fairness testing
controls.objective: Test AI outcomes for unfair differences across groups before release and periodically in production.
guidance: Define protected and relevant groups and fairness metrics per use case
Pre-release fairness testing with documented thresholds and sign-off
Re-test after retraining and when population or context drifts

controls.title: Verification, validation and adversarial testing
controls.objective: Verify AI meets its requirements and red-team it against misuse, jailbreaks and failure modes before release.
guidance: Test plan covering accuracy, robustness, safety and security acceptance criteria
Red-team exercises using OWASP LLM and Agentic Top 10 scenarios
Re-run regression suites for every model, prompt or tool change

sector_notes.healthcare: Clinical validation should be prospective where outputs inform care decisions.

controls.title: Prompt injection and hidden context protection
controls.objective: Treat all external and retrieved content as untrusted and stop it from overriding system instructions or extracting hidden context.
guidance: Separate and label trusted instructions from untrusted content (documents, web, email, images)
Input screening for direct, indirect and cross-modal injection
Constrain agent objectives so retrieved content cannot change goals without approval

controls.title: Output validation and content safeguards
controls.objective: Validate and constrain model output before it reaches users or downstream systems, including code and commands.
guidance: Encode and validate output before passing to browsers, databases, shells or APIs
Sandbox any execution of model-generated code
Content safety filters and grounding / citation checks for factual claims

controls.title: Agent permissions and least agency
controls.objective: Give AI agents only the tools, permissions and autonomy their task needs, with scoped identities and authenticated agent-to-agent communication.
guidance: Tool allow-lists and per-tool scopes; no broad standing credentials
Distinct, short-lived non-human identities for agents; no inherited user super-privileges
Authenticate and integrity-protect inter-agent messages; limit delegation depth

sector_notes.manufacturing: Agents that can act on OT or production systems need hard safety interlocks.

controls.title: Human oversight and intervention
controls.objective: Ensure competent people can understand, override, stop or reverse AI decisions, proportionate to risk.
guidance: Define where human-in-the-loop, on-the-loop or post-hoc review applies per use case
Approval gates for high-impact agent actions; stop / kill switch tested regularly
Design approvals to resist rubber-stamping and manipulation (clear context, no dark patterns)

sector_notes.healthcare: Clinician remains the decision-maker; guard against automation bias.

controls.title: Transparency to users and AI disclosure
controls.objective: Tell people when they are interacting with AI or seeing AI-generated content, and what the system can and cannot do.
guidance: Clear AI-interaction notices and labelling or marking of synthetic content
User-facing documentation of capabilities, limitations and appropriate use
Information for affected people on how to query or contest outcomes

controls.title: Explainability and technical documentation
controls.objective: Document how AI systems are designed, built and behave so that outcomes can be explained and compliance demonstrated.
guidance: Model and system cards covering purpose, data, design choices, performance and limits
Explanation methods appropriate to the audience (regulator, user, affected person)
Keep documentation current with each material change

sector_notes.finance: Adverse credit decisions need explanations customers can understand.

controls.title: Event logging and traceability
controls.objective: Log AI inputs, outputs, decisions, tool calls and agent actions so behaviour can be reconstructed and investigated.
guidance: Define what is logged per lifecycle phase, with retention aligned to legal requirements
Correlate agent plans, tool calls and approvals in one trace
Protect logs from tampering and redact sensitive data where needed

controls.title: AI supply chain and third-party model assurance
controls.objective: Assess and govern third-party models, data sets, tools, plugins and AI vendors, with clear allocation of responsibilities.
guidance: AI-specific vendor due diligence (model provenance, training data, security testing, data use terms)
AI bill of materials for models, data sets and agent tools / MCP servers
Contractual allocation of provider / deployer responsibilities and incident cooperation

sector_notes.finance: Treat critical AI providers as ICT third-party risk (e.g. DORA register).

controls.title: Model and AI infrastructure security
controls.objective: Protect models, weights, vector stores, agent runtimes and compute from unauthorised access, theft and tampering.
guidance: Harden and segment AI infrastructure; secure model registries and artefact signing
Access control and monitoring on vector databases and embedding pipelines
Run agent code execution in isolated, least-privilege sandboxes

controls.title: Resource abuse and cascading failure protection
controls.objective: Prevent uncontrolled consumption, denial of service, model extraction and runaway agent loops.
guidance: Rate limits, quotas and budget alerts per user, app and agent
Loop, recursion and timeout limits for agents; circuit breakers between agents
Monitor for extraction patterns and anomalous usage

controls.title: Deployment gates and change management
controls.objective: Release AI only through defined readiness gates, and control changes to models, prompts, tools and data.
guidance: Go-live checklist linking risk assessment, testing, documentation and oversight sign-off
Version control for models, prompts, agent configurations and guardrails
Rollback plan and staged rollout for material changes

controls.title: Post-deployment monitoring and drift management
controls.objective: Monitor AI performance, safety, fairness and behaviour in production and act on drift or emerging issues.
guidance: KPIs and thresholds for accuracy, hallucination, fairness and safety events
Behavioural monitoring for agents acting outside expected patterns
Feedback loop from users and incidents into the risk register

controls.title: AI incident management and reporting
controls.objective: Detect, respond to, learn from and report AI incidents, including regulatory notification where required.
guidance: Extend incident taxonomy and playbooks to AI-specific harms and agent failures
Criteria and timelines for internal escalation and external / regulatory reporting
Post-incident reviews feeding back into controls and testing

controls.title: AI literacy and responsible-use training
controls.objective: Give staff the knowledge to use, oversee and challenge AI appropriately for their role.
guidance: Role-based AI literacy curriculum (all staff, developers, overseers, executives)
Training on over-reliance, verification of outputs and recognising manipulation by agents
Track completion and refresh as tools and rules change

controls.title: Environmental and compute footprint management
controls.objective: Measure and manage the energy and resource footprint of AI development and use.
guidance: Track compute and energy use for training and inference where feasible
Prefer right-sized models; include footprint in build-vs-buy decisions
Report footprint alongside other sustainability metrics

controls.title: Dangerous capability and misuse safeguards
controls.objective: Prevent AI capabilities from being used for fraud, manipulation, cyber offence or other serious misuse.
guidance: Usage policies and acceptable-use enforcement for AI tools and APIs
Capability evaluations and abuse monitoring for high-impact models and agents
Controls against deepfake and impersonation fraud in customer channels

sector_notes.finance: Voice and video deepfakes are a live payment-fraud vector.

controls.title: Customer and downstream deployer information
controls.objective: Give customers and downstream deployers what they need to use the AI system safely and meet their own obligations.
guidance: Instructions for use, known limitations and required oversight measures
Channel for customers to report issues and receive updates
Clear statement of which party holds which obligations
